newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares rebound, tracking Dow to close up.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares rebound, tracking Dow to close up.

text.p: Brazilian shares pared early losses to end 1.69 percent higher on Monday, as a rebound on Wall Street and easing concerns over a state debt probe brought investors back to the market late in the session, brokers said.
The Bovespa index .BVSP of the 49 most active shares closed at 8,978 points after the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa) divided the index by 10 to make it easier for investors to read it.
Volume was a moderate 446.4 million reais ($424 million), less than the bolsa's recent daily average of $600 million.

Shares fell more than one percent earlier in the session amid concern over a Senate inquiry into a multi-million fraud scheme involving state and municipal bonds, traders said. Later, local stocks recouped losses as fears that the probe could broaden to an inquiry into Brazil's entire financial sector appeared to diminish, they added.
"Fears that the state debt probe would hit the whole financial sector apparently dissipated," said Bruno Pena, equities desk manager at Rio-based Banco Omega.
Analysts expect the market to firm on Tuesday with top blue-chips leading the rise.

Federal power utility Eletrobras rose 2.31 percent to 488 reais.
State mining concern Companhia Vale do Rio Doce fell 0.72 percent to 27.70 reais after the stock's recent gains. Tender documents for the company's sale are expected to be released on Wednesday.
Vale's privatization is expected to begin in April.
The power sector index .IEE, comprising the nine most liquid stocks of the electrical industry, rose 0.15 percent to 2,542 points.
